memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user stores wrapping paper and empty gift boxes on the upper shelf of the bedroom closet.
From photographs, the user discovered that they had given their mother the same type of kitchen item two years in a row.
This year, the user went to the market with their mother and let her choose a needed item directly.
The user once ordered a gift late and had it delivered the day after the gathering.
The next year, the user checked the expected delivery date and ordered one week before the gathering.
The user did not put names on wrapped boxes and handed their older sister and younger brother each other's gifts.
The next time the user wrapped gifts, they wrote the recipient on the bottom of each box.
The user's younger brother welcomes a snack the family can share immediately more than an item for his use alone.
The local agent can find past gift records and flag duplicates but cannot know what is needed this year.
Year-end deliveries may take longer than usual or have their expected dates changed.

analysis.overview: The frames cover independent domains: the reference records sleep, coffee timing, bedroom comfort, and tired-evening behavior, while the compared records gift selection, preparation, delivery, family preferences, and agent limits. No claims address the same operational decision closely enough for a cross-frame relation.
